tex_content.html:
Proposition
[the matrix exponential is the integral curve of a left-invariant field]

Source: petersen:page-0155, petersen:page-0156 ↗ def:pet-ch4-lie-algebra-exp

On a matrix Lie group, $\tfrac {d}{dt}\big|_{t=t_0}e^{tX}=X|_{e^{t_0X}}$; more generally $t\mapsto \exp (tX)$ is the unique integral curve of $X$ through $e$ because $t\mapsto \exp (tX)$ is a homomorphism $\mathbb {R}\to G$ with derivative $X|_e$ at $t=0$.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch4-matrix-exp-integral-curve

\sketch From $e^{(t_0+s)X}=L_{e^{t_0X}}(e^{sX})$,

\[ \frac d{dt}\Big|_{t=t_0}e^{tX} =(DL_{e^{t_0X}})_eX=X|_{e^{t_0X}}. \]

For an arbitrary Lie group, the same conclusion follows because $t\mapsto \exp (tX)$ is the unique one-parameter subgroup with initial derivative $X$.

□
